item.title: Beyond Automation: AI, Accounting, Finance, and the Future of Labor
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Aminu Sualihu, Zayed University

This special issue examines how artificial intelligence is transforming accounting, finance, and the workplace. The call addresses both the opportunities and challenges created by AI adoption, including innovations in financial reporting and decision-making alongside concerns about governance, ethics, and workforce impacts.

The special issue welcomes interdisciplinary research exploring AI's role across multiple dimensions: financial systems and corporate governance, human capital management and job design, labor market dynamics, and responsible technology implementation. It seeks to integrate perspectives from accounting, finance, and related fields to understand how organizations can harness AI's potential while addressing economic and societal consequences for workers and labor markets.

Appel publié par International Journal of Managerial Finance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Artificial intelligence in accounting and corporate finance
  • AI-enabled financial reporting and disclosures
  • AI, corporate governance, and organizational accountability
  • AI, labor markets, employment, and job redesign
  • Wage inequality, labor exploitation, and worker well-being in the AI era
  • AI, diversity, equity, inclusion, and workplace fairness
  • Public policy, AI regulation, and labor related governance issues
  • The societal implications of AI for accounting, finance, and the future of work

Timeline

  • November 30, 2026: Opening date for manuscripts submissions
  • March 31, 2027: Closing date for manuscripts submission

item.title: Entrepreneurship and the Creation of Decent Work for All
item.content:encoded:
This multi-journal collection addresses the relationship between entrepreneurship and the creation of decent work, aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8. The collection recognizes that societal changes, environmental crises, and economic disruptions significantly impact employment quality and labor market conditions, and that entrepreneurship may serve as a critical mechanism for generating productive employment and fair working conditions.

The collection seeks to gather diverse scholarly perspectives on how entrepreneurship can contribute to achieving full and productive employment with decent wages, improved labor market access, and better job opportunities. Submissions may be research or review articles and will undergo rigorous peer review according to each participating journal's standards, with accepted articles published in the submitting journal and highlighted in the collection.

Appel publié par Small Business Economics. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Equal pay for work of equal value
  • Gender discrimination in employment
  • Immigration and employment
  • Labor shortages after COVID-19
  • Modern slavery and child labor
  • Labor policy
  • Entrepreneurial enterprises, SMEs, and family businesses
  • Global entrepreneurial firms
  • Remote work
  • Opportunity entrepreneurship
  • Measuring externalities of new businesses
